messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: embeddings route 'embeds-hot' increased error rate to 18% and p95 latency jumped to 3.2s across us-west-2. Auto-scaling failing due to OOM on a subset of GPU workers. Paging dev-oncall @devin :rotating_light:

devin: On it, pulling dashboard now. Seeing a big fanout from a single API key (acct: acme-marketing).

alex: acme-marketing is hitting batch size=1024 jobs, token lengths ~8k. That explains OOMs. They also hit rerank calls chained post-embed.

jamie: tagging infra: their jobs are hammering kv-cache + long prefix reads. We probably need quick perimeter carve before full capacity impact.

devin: Agreed. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle embeddings for non-enterprise keys 2) prioritize chat traffic 3) carve dedicated capacity for critical customers (if possible) 4) temporarily disable automatic large-batch path for embeds.

morgan: Notify CS for high-touch customers + run risk assessment. Priya, can you confirm which accounts are high priority?

priya: ACME and BetaRetail are on enterprise support. ACME is the one currently spiking. Reached out to them to ask for pause on bulk jobs.

devin: Executing surgical quota tweaks now. Will post changes and rollback plan.

alex: Commands I'm running (prod-admin):
```bash
# reduce per-key embeddings QPS for non-enterprise
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/quotas/set -d '{"route":"embeds-hot","scope":"non-enterprise","qps":5}' -H 'Auth: admin-token'

# deprioritize non-chat routes in the router
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/router/prioritize -d '{"lower_priority":["embeds-hot","rerank"],"raise_priority":["chat"]}'
```

jamie: Also toggling feature flag to disable large-batch fast path (quantized streaming) for now:
```json
{"feature":"embed-large-batch-optim","enabled":false}
```

support-bot: NOTE: quota change applied to scope non-enterprise on embeds-hot: qps=5 (effective immediately).

devin: Observability check: error rate down to 6% after throttle, p95 to 1.1s — looks promising but still elevated. Need to smooth short-term throughput to avoid oscillation.

morgan: For routing, can we carve a small dedicated slice for enterprise chat + embeds so BetaRetail/ACME keep minimal service?

alex: We can reserve 10% of pool for enterprise by tagging kernels. Doing a route carve: 
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://admin.internal/capacity/carve -d '{"tag":"enterprise-reserve","percent":10,"routes":["chat","embeds-hot"]}'
```

support-bot: capacity carve queued, will apply in ~90s.

priya: ACME confirmed they can delay one batch job, they appreciate the carve but asked for ETA on full restore.

devin: ETA depends on persistent load reduction. If spike stops, we can restore in ~20m. Plan B: if carve isn't enough, we move to stricter per-route qps (embeds non-enterprise -> 2 qps) and stall rerank calls for non-enterprise.

sasha: Quick note: rerank single-threaded workers are saturating RPCs to scoring service. Might need to throttle rerank specifically.

alex: Implementing rerank throttle for non-enterprise now: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/quotas/set -d '{"route":"rerank","scope":"non-enterprise","qps":1}'
```

support-bot: rerank non-enterprise qps=1 applied.

devin: After these changes: embeddings errors 2.6%, p95 850ms, overall token throughput down 28% — acceptable for now. Keeping incident open to monitor 30m.

priya: Logged customer comms for ACME and BetaRetail. ACME asked for an SRE post-incident summary and steps taken.

morgan: Post-incident action items: - Evaluate throttling thresholds per-tenant - Add auto-detection for large-batch jobs that escalate to CS before running - Improve docs for customers on large-embed best practices

jamie: Also add a playbook step to carve enterprise slices automatically when OOM signature detected on GPU cluster.

devin: Handoff to next oncall @alex in 25m; I'll stay on monitoring for 30m then hand over formally. If anyone sees anomalies ping me directly.

alex: Acknowledged, taking over watches. Will keep the carve in place until next check-in.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (per-endpoint qps tweaks, rerank throttle, feature-flag rollback for large-batch path). Severity reduced to P2.

devin: Closing note: Keep an eye on queued jobs backlog — if it spikes again we'll need to coordinate customer pauses rather than more throttles to avoid long tail SLA hits.

priya: Will follow up with ACME for exact job ids and proposed schedule for resubmitting.

morgan: Thanks everyone. Filing a short postmortem after stabilization with the customer timeline and mitigation timeline. :thumbsup:
